column3: The Hebrew calls the people David’s bone and flesh; BSB uses flesh and blood.
The Hebrew says yesterday and the day before yesterday and repeats My people Israel in the final clause; BSB uses times past and then a pronoun.
The Hebrew repeats Hebron and David’s name and describes mediation through Samuel’s hand; BSB omits the repeated place and name and simply says through Samuel.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew promises the roles of head and commander separately; BSB combines them as chief commander.
The Hebrew has active plural naming agents; BSB expresses the naming passively.

The Hebrew names the Millo and speaks of the surrounding area without explicitly naming a wall; BSB has supporting terraces and the surrounding wall. Joab’s restoration is expressed with a verb meaning to make alive.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes strengthening themselves with him in his kingship to make him king; BSB describes bolstering and strengthening his kingdom without a separate king-making purpose.
The Hebrew introduces the number of the mighty men; BSB calls this their list.
The Hebrew says after him; BSB specifies next in command.
The Hebrew says the people fled; BSB specifies troops.
The Hebrew leaves the defenders unnamed; BSB identifies them as Eleazar and David. The LORD’s victory is expressed by repeating the salvation word as verb and noun.
Close to the Hebrew.

Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew separately says the men carried the water and brought it to David; BSB combines this as bringing it back to him.
The Hebrew repeats with their souls and does not repeat David’s name in his refusal; BSB describes risking their lives and explicitly names David.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls Benaiah the son of a valiant man; BSB directly calls Benaiah a man of valor.
The Hebrew initially says he struck the Egyptian and later says he killed him; BSB uses killed in both places and supplies Benaiah’s name.
The Hebrew says a name belonged to him among the three mighty men; BSB presents this as winning a name alongside them.
The Hebrew says he was honored above the Thirty; BSB says most honored among them.
